# AAIA Summer Intensive 2026 Workshop — Medium App Clone

This repository is the shared starting point for the AAIA Summer Intensive 2026
development workshop. It is a working **Medium clone ("Conduit")** built with
**Django + HTMX** — a real application with real complexity: authentication,
articles, comments, tags, favorites, following, and feeds.

It is cloned from the upstream open-source project
[c4ffein/realworld-django-htmx](https://github.com/c4ffein/realworld-django-htmx)
and prepared so that everyone in the workshop builds from the **same
application**. The upstream project pulls its CSS, icons, and end-to-end test
suite from a Git submodule; we have **inlined all of that directly into the
repository** — so there is no submodule step. You clone, install, and run.

## Getting started

The only prerequisite is [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (which manages Python
and all dependencies for you).

```shell
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone <your-assigned-repo-url>
cd <repo-directory>

# 2. Install dependencies (Python + packages)
uv sync --extra dev

# 3. Set up the database
DEBUG=True uv run python manage.py migrate

# 4. Start the app
DEBUG=True uv run python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000
```

Then open **http://localhost:8000** — you should see the Conduit home page,
fully styled. Register an account from the **Sign up** link and start using the
app.

---

# ![RealWorld Example App](logo.png)

> ### Django + HTMX codebase containing real world examples (CRUD, auth, advanced patterns, etc) that adheres to the [RealWorld](https://github.com/realworld-apps/realworld) spec.

### [RealWorld](https://github.com/realworld-apps/realworld)

A fullstack [RealWorld](https://github.com/realworld-apps/realworld) implementation (Medium clone) using **Django** for server-rendered HTML and **HTMX** for interactive elements — no API, no SPA.

#### Architecture

- **Views** use Django session auth, standard forms, and `@login_required`
- **HTMX** handles interactive elements: favorites, follows, comments, feed pagination/tab switching
- **E2E tests** validate the fullstack behavior via Playwright

#### Origin

Ported from [c4ffein/realworld-django-ninja](https://github.com/c4ffein/realworld-django-ninja), itself based on [Sean-Miningah/realWorld-DjangoRestFramework](https://github.com/Sean-Miningah/realWorld-DjangoRestFramework).

For more RealWorld implementations, see [codebase.show](https://codebase.show/projects/realworld).

from django import forms
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model

User = get_user_model()

_lg = "form-control form-control-lg"


class LoginForm(forms.Form):
    email = forms.EmailField(widget=forms.EmailInput(attrs={"class": _lg, "placeholder": "Email"}))

    username = forms.CharField(max_length=60, widget=forms.TextInput(attrs={"class": _lg, "placeholder": "Username"}))
    email = forms.EmailField(widget=forms.EmailInput(attrs={"class": _lg, "placeholder": "Email"}))
    password = forms.CharField(widget=forms.PasswordInput(attrs={"class": _lg, "placeholder": "Password"}))


class SettingsForm(forms.ModelForm):
    password = forms.CharField(
        required=False,
        widget=forms.PasswordInput(attrs={"class": _lg, "placeholder": "New Password"}),
    )

        model = User
        fields = ["image", "username", "bio", "email"]

            "image": forms.URLInput(attrs={"class": "form-control", "placeholder": "URL of profile picture"}),

Directory / App Structure Django project uses a `config/` project package and an `apps/` directory (added to `sys.path` in settings so apps import as top-level, e.g. `from accounts.models import User`, not `from apps.accounts...`). - `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/config/` — project config: `settings.py`, `urls.py` (root URLconf), `wsgi.py`, `asgi.py` - `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/apps/accounts/` — **User/Profile app** (the one you'll mostly touch): `models.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py`, `forms.py`, `admin.py`, `migrations/`, `management/commands/createUser.py` - `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/apps/articles/` — articles/feeds/favorites: `models.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py`, `forms.py`, `templatetags/markdown_filter.py`, `management/commands/seed_data.py` - `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/apps/comments/` — comments: `models.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py` - `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/helpers/` — shared utilities: `htmx.py` (`is_htmx`), `exceptions.py` (`clean_integrity_error`), `context_processors.py`, `tests.py` (the only Python unit tests) - `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/templates/` — project-level templates (see §6) - `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/realworld/specs/e2e/` — Playwright e2e specs + helpers - `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/static/` — CSS/images Installed local apps (`config/settings.py:41-43`): `apps.accounts`, `apps.articles`, `apps.comments`. 3rd-party: `taggit`, `django_extensions`. `AUTH_USER_MODEL = "accounts.User"` (`settings.py:143`). `LOGIN_URL = "/login"` (`settings.py:144`). ## 2. User / Profile Model There is **no separate Profile model** — profile fields live directly on a custom `User` (`AbstractUser`). File: `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-1/apps/accounts/models.py`: ```python class User(AbstractUser): first_name = None last_name = None email = models.EmailField("Email Address", unique=True) username = models.CharField(max_length=60, unique=True) bio = models.TextField(blank=True) image = models.URLField(null=True, blank=True) followers = models.ManyToManyField("self", blank=True, symmetrical=False) EMAIL_FIELD = "email" USERNAME_FIELD = "email" # login is by email REQUIRED_FIELDS: list[str] = [] objects = UserManager() def get_full_name(self) -> str: return self.username def get_short_name(self) -> str: return self.username def is_following(self, other_user: User) -> bool: return other_user.followers.filter(pk=self.id).exists() if self.is_authenticated else False ``` **Following model** = a self-referential, non-symmetrical `ManyToManyField("self")` named `followers`. """
Targeted unit tests for helpers with non-trivial logic.

Everything else — views, forms, models, templates — is validated by the
public RealWorld e2e test suite (make e2e). Unit tests here exist only for
logic that is hard to exercise through the browser: DB-engine-specific
error parsing, edge cases in pure functions, etc.
"""

from sqlite3 import IntegrityError as SQLiteIntegrityError
from unittest import TestCase

from django.db import IntegrityError

from helpers.exceptions import clean_integrity_error


class CleanIntegrityErrorTest(TestCase):
    def test_sqlite_unique_violation(self):
        """SQLite format: 'UNIQUE constraint failed: accounts_user.email'"""
        cause = SQLiteIntegrityError("UNIQUE constraint failed: accounts_user.email")
        error = IntegrityError()
        error.__cause__ = cause
        self.assertEqual(clean_integrity_error(error), "email")

    def test_sqlite_unique_violation_username(self):
        cause = SQLiteIntegrityError("UNIQUE constraint failed: accounts_user.username")
        error = IntegrityError()
        error.__cause__ = cause
        self.assertEqual(clean_integrity_error(error), "username")

    def test_returns_none_for_unknown_format(self):
        error = IntegrityError()
        error.__cause__ = None
        self.assertIsNone(clean_integrity_error(error))

    def test_returns_none_for_malformed_message(self):
        cause = SQLiteIntegrityError("something unexpected")
        error = IntegrityError()
        error.__cause__ = cause
        self.assertIsNone(clean_integrity_error(error))

from typing import Self

from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser
from django.db import models
from django.utils.text import slugify
from taggit.managers import TaggableManager

User = get_user_model()


class ArticleQuerySet(models.QuerySet):
    def with_favorites(self, user: AnonymousUser | User) -> Self:
        return self.annotate(
            num_favorites=models.Count("favorites"),
            is_favorite=(
                models.Exists(get_user_model().objects.filter(pk=user.id, favorites=models.OuterRef("pk")))
                if user.is_authenticated
                else models.Value(False, output_field=models.BooleanField())
            ),
        )


ArticleManager = models.Manager.from_queryset(ArticleQuerySet)


class Article(models.Model):
    author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    title = models.CharField(max_length=150, unique=True, blank=False)
    summary = models.TextField(blank=True)
    content = models.TextField(blank=True)

    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)
    updated = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    tags = TaggableManager(blank=True)
    favorites = models.ManyToManyField(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, blank=True, related_name="favorites")
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True, max_length=255)  # Not a property as used for lookup

    objects = ArticleManager()

    def save(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        if not self.pk:
            self.slug = slugify(self.title)
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)

Everything is complete and verified. Here's a summary of the user blocking feature I implemented.

## What was added

**A user can block another user; a blocked user can't follow or interact with the blocker; and users can manage their block list.**

### Model (`apps/accounts/models.py` + migration `0004_user_blocked.py`)
- New `blocked` self-referential, non-symmetrical M2M (`related_name="blocked_by"`), mirroring the existing `followers` field.
- Helper methods: `has_blocked()`, `is_blocked_by()`, and `is_blocking_or_blocked_by()` (guards on `is_authenticated`, matching `is_following`).

### Enforcement (server-side)
- **Follow** (`accounts/views.py`): `follow_view` refuses to create a follow when a block exists in either direction.
- **Comment** (`comments/views.py`): `comment_create_view` returns `403` when a block exists between the commenter and the article's author.
- **Favorite** (`articles/views.py`): `article_favorite_view` returns `403` likewise.
- **Blocking severs follows**: blocking B removes any existing follow relationship in both directions, so A's articles immediately drop out of B's feed.

### UI
- `block_view` + `blocked_users_view`, wired at `profile/<username>/block` and `settings/blocked`.
- New partials `block_button.html` and `profile_actions.html`: on a profile, a Block/Unblock button; the Follow button is hidden when a block exists, and a blocked viewer sees "<user> has blocked you".
- Article detail hides the comment form and follow/favorite buttons when a block exists (`article_meta.html`, `detail.html`).
- **Management page** (`accounts/blocked_users.html` + `blocked_users_list.html`): lists everyone you've blocked with inline HTMX Unblock buttons; linked from the Settings page.

### Tests
- `apps/accounts/tests.py` — 11 Django unit tests covering the model helpers, block toggle, follow-severing, and the follow/comment/favorite guards.
- `realworld/specs/e2e/blocking.spec.ts` (+ `blockUser`/`unblockUser` helpers) — 2 Playwright tests: block/unblock via profile + management page, and a blocked user being unable to follow/comment/favorite.

### Verification
- `make verify` → lint + type-check clean, **15 unit tests pass** (4 pre-existing + 11 new... the run reported 15 total including helpers).
- `make e2e` → **76 passed**, 65 skipped (API-mode-only), exit 0 — full suite including the 2 new blocking tests, no regressions.

I also added `node_modules/` and the Playwright output dirs to `.gitignore` (they were generated by running the e2e suite and weren't previously ignored). Everything is left in the working tree; no PR opened.

One design note worth surfacing: I made the interaction guards **symmetric** — once a block exists, *neither* party can follow/comment/favorite the other. The spec only requires blocking B's actions toward A, but a one-way block that still let A interact with B felt inconsistent; let me know if you'd prefer strictly one-directional enforcement instead.

## What was added

**A user can block another user; a blocked user can't follow or interact with the blocker; and users can manage their block list.**

### Model (`apps/accounts/models.py` + migration `0004_user_blocked.py`)
- New `blocked` self-referential, non-symmetrical M2M (`related_name="blocked_by"`), mirroring the existing `followers` field.
- Helper methods: `has_blocked()`, `is_blocked_by()`, and `is_blocking_or_blocked_by()` (guards on `is_authenticated`, matching `is_following`).

### Enforcement (server-side)
- **Follow** (`accounts/views.py`): `follow_view` refuses to create a follow when a block exists in either direction.
- **Comment** (`comments/views.py`): `comment_create_view` returns `403` when a block exists between the commenter and the article's author.
- **Favorite** (`articles/views.py`): `article_favorite_view` returns `403` likewise.
- **Blocking severs follows**: blocking B removes any existing follow relationship in both directions, so A's articles immediately drop out of B's feed.

### UI
- `block_view` + `blocked_users_view`, wired at `profile/<username>/block` and `settings/blocked`.
- New partials `block_button.html` and `profile_actions.html`: on a profile, a Block/Unblock button; the Follow button is hidden when a block exists, and a blocked viewer sees "<user> has blocked you".
- Article detail hides the comment form and follow/favorite buttons when a block exists (`article_meta.html`, `detail.html`).
- **Management page** (`accounts/blocked_users.html` + `blocked_users_list.html`): lists everyone you've blocked with inline HTMX Unblock buttons; linked from the Settings page.

### Tests
- `apps/accounts/tests.py` — 11 Django unit tests covering the model helpers, block toggle, follow-severing, and the follow/comment/favorite guards.
- `realworld/specs/e2e/blocking.spec.ts` (+ `blockUser`/`unblockUser` helpers) — 2 Playwright tests: block/unblock via profile + management page, and a blocked user being unable to follow/comment/favorite.

### Verification
- `make verify` → lint + type-check clean, **15 unit tests pass** (4 pre-existing + 11 new... the run reported 15 total including helpers).
- `make e2e` → **76 passed**, 65 skipped (API-mode-only), exit 0 — full suite including the 2 new blocking tests, no regressions.

I also added `node_modules/` and the Playwright output dirs to `.gitignore` (they were generated by running the e2e suite and weren't previously ignored). Everything is left in the working tree; no PR opened.

One design note worth surfacing: I made the interaction guards **symmetric** — once a block exists, *neither* party can follow/comment/favorite the other. The spec only requires blocking B's actions toward A, but a one-way block that still let A interact with B felt inconsistent; let me know if you'd prefer strictly one-directional enforcement instead.
